CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Balangan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Head hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Balangan Regency.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the regional people's representative institution of Balangan Regency which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Office or Agency is an Office or Agency whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the field of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region.
6. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
8. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
9. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a direct line upward or downward and a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child.
10. Parent is a biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
11. Protection of women and children is an effort to prevent and handle all forms of acts of violence including neglect and trafficking in persons that violate the human rights of women and children, as well as providing basic and specific services for the needs of women and children in the conditions and situations they experience.
12. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
13. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Empowerment of women and children is an effort to strengthen human rights, improve quality of life and increase the participation of women and children in their social interactions.
15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
17. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
18. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
21. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related offices, vertical agencies, and the community, in the context of implementing activities for the prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.

Letter a
What is meant by “physical violence” is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person’s body, miscarriage, fainting, and/or causes death. Letter b
What is meant by “sexual violence” is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. Letter c
What is meant by “psychological violence” is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. Letter d
What is meant by intimidation is the act of ordering or prohibiting by means of threatening or restraining to cause harm so that the victim is unable to make choices for their best interests. Letter e
What is meant by forced eviction is the act of ordering by force or with physical force not to be in a safe place or position as is the right possessed by a person to a place suitable for them. Letter f
What is meant by deprivation of liberty is the act of eliminating the right to live based on the best interests of a person. Letter g
What is meant by neglect is:
 a. actions that result in the failure to fulfill a child’s needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social; b. actions of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate; c. actions that neglect a person within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and
 d. actions that result in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. Letter h
What is meant by “exploitation” includes:
 a. actions that exploit a child economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; b. actions with or without the victim’s consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues, or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
 c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all prostitution or indecency activities. What is meant by “trafficking in persons” is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage, or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE.
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Balangan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Head hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Balangan Regency.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the regional people's representative institution of Balangan Regency which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Office or Agency is an Office or Agency whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the field of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region.
6. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
8. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
9. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a direct line upward or downward and a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child.
10. Parent is a biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
11. Protection of women and children is an effort to prevent and handle all forms of acts of violence including neglect and trafficking in persons that violate the human rights of women and children, as well as providing basic and specific services for the needs of women and children in the conditions and situations they experience.
12. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
13. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Empowerment of women and children is an effort to strengthen human rights, improve quality of life and increase the participation of women and children in their social interactions.
15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
17. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
18. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
21. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related offices, vertical agencies, and the community, in the context of implementing activities for the prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.

Article 19 (1) The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region.
(2) The community is authorized to actively supervise the implementation of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region.
(3) The authority of the community as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of:
a. providing input; b. submitting questions and obtaining answers from regional government officials who are responsible;
c. requesting realization and concrete activities from those assigned with duties and authority;

Article 21
(1) Funding for the Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget.
(2) In addition to funds from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, funding may come from grants or contributions from third parties that are non-binding.
(3) Technically and for the operation of the Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children, it shall be placed in the budget line of the Agency determined by the Regent.
(4) The allocation of funds by the Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children shall be based on the established work program.
(5) Accountability for the use of funds for the implementation of protection of women and children shall be in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

ACTING REGENT OF BALANGAN,

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF BALANGAN REGENCY NUMBER 3 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and enforced to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for such women. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, return, and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community.
The protection and empowerment of women and children currently becomes a focus in development. Women and children are usually made into one unit within the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the respective scope of each form of handling, namely women and children do not become a unit. In that context, regionally related to women and children, regional regulations must be present concerning: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. These four regional regulations are a package that must be regulated by the Regional Government in accordance with authority.

REGIONAL HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES OF BALANGAN REGENCY
REGENT OF BALANGAN
DECIDES:
To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING PROTECTION

CHAPTER X REGIONAL ACTION PLAN
Article 20 (1) The Regent may establish a regional action plan related to the protection and empowerment of women and children.
(2) The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1) is manifested in the joint commitment of all elements in the region to implement the protection and empowerment of women and children and eliminate all forms of violence, neglect and human trafficking.
SUPPLEMENT TO THE REGIONAL GAZETTE OF BALANGAN REGENCY NUMBER 117

Article 22 This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of its promulgation. In order that every person may know of it, it is ordered that this Regional Regulation be promulgated by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Balangan Regency.

CHAPTER VII INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS
Article 10
(1) In order to provide services to women and children victims of violence, neglect and human trafficking, the Regional Government establishes an Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A).
(2) The Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) is positioned as an independent institution.
Article 11
(1) The Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) has the authority to administer protection for women and children.
(2) The duty of the Regional Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) is to implement protection for women and children in accordance with the provisions stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
Article 12
The membership of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) consists of elements from related agencies, vertical institutions, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, researchers, academics and religious figures, customary figures, community figures and activists for the protection of women and children in the region.
Article 13
(1) The Regent establishes the Management of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A).
(2) The establishment of the Management as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Regent's Decree including the secretariat structure of the management and provision of supporting facilities for the implementation of activities.
Article 14
(1) The Management of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) consists of leadership elements and members stipulated by Regent's Decree.
(2) Leadership elements comprise:
a. chairperson;
b. secretary; and
c. treasurer.
(3) Membership elements are divided into the form of:
a. service division;
b. information division;
c. assistance division;
d. education and training division.
Article 15
(1) The Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children, in carrying out its functions, builds a working network with:
a. Police;
b. Prosecutor's Office;
c. Court;
d. Witness and Victim Protection Institution;
e. Hospital/Community Health Center;
f. Other institutions that have similar objectives.
(2) In addition to building a working network as referred to in paragraph (1), cooperation may be conducted with:
a. Government;
b. Provincial Government;
c. Other Regency/City Governments; and
d. Non-Governmental Institutions.
e. International institutions whose existence is recognized.
(3) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is set forth in the form of a joint agreement.
Article 16
(1) The Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children establishes partnerships with the business sector for support in administering protection for women and children in the Regional territory.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are in the form of:
a. information and opening of employment opportunities;
b. provision of education and job training;
c. provision of educational assistance for women and children victims of violence; and
d. provision of capital assistance for independent businesses.
Article 17
The Regent as the person responsible for the protection and empowerment of regional women and children has the authority to make changes to the management or dismissal of members if the existing management or members do not carry out their roles and functions.

CHAPTER VII INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS
Article 10
(1) In order to provide services to women and children victims of violence, neglect and human trafficking, the Regional Government establishes an Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A).
(2) The Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) is positioned as an independent institution.
Article 11
(1) The Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) has the authority to administer protection for women and children.
(2) The duty of the Regional Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) is to implement protection for women and children in accordance with the provisions stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
Article 12
The membership of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) consists of elements from related agencies, vertical institutions, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, researchers, academics and religious figures, customary figures, community figures and activists for the protection of women and children in the region.
Article 13
(1) The Regent establishes the Management of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A).
(2) The establishment of the Management as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Regent's Decree including the secretariat structure of the management and provision of supporting facilities for the implementation of activities.
Article 14
(1) The Management of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) consists of leadership elements and members stipulated by Regent's Decree.
(2) Leadership elements comprise:
a. chairperson;
b. secretary; and
c. treasurer.
(3) Membership elements are divided into the form of:
a. service division;
b. information division;
c. assistance division;
d. education and training division.
Article 15
(1) The Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children, in carrying out its functions, builds a working network with:
a. Police;
b. Prosecutor's Office;
c. Court;
d. Witness and Victim Protection Institution;
e. Hospital/Community Health Center;
f. Other institutions that have similar objectives.
(2) In addition to building a working network as referred to in paragraph (1), cooperation may be conducted with:
a. Government;
b. Provincial Government;
c. Other Regency/City Governments; and
d. Non-Governmental Institutions.
e. International institutions whose existence is recognized.
(3) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is set forth in the form of a joint agreement.
Article 16
(1) The Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children establishes partnerships with the business sector for support in administering protection for women and children in the Regional territory.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are in the form of:
a. information and opening of employment opportunities;
b. provision of education and job training;
c. provision of educational assistance for women and children victims of violence; and
d. provision of capital assistance for independent businesses.
Article 17
The Regent as the person responsible for the protection and empowerment of regional women and children has the authority to make changes to the management or dismissal of members if the existing management or members do not carry out their roles and functions.

WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE.
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Balangan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Head hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Balangan Regency.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the regional people's representative institution of Balangan Regency which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Office or Agency is an Office or Agency whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the field of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region.
6. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
8. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
9. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a direct line upward or downward and a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child.
10. Parent is a biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
11. Protection of women and children is an effort to prevent and handle all forms of acts of violence including neglect and trafficking in persons that violate the human rights of women and children, as well as providing basic and specific services for the needs of women and children in the conditions and situations they experience.
12. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
13. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Empowerment of women and children is an effort to strengthen human rights, improve quality of life and increase the participation of women and children in their social interactions.
15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
17. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
18. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
21. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related offices, vertical agencies, and the community, in the context of implementing activities for the prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.

CHAPTER V SERVICES
Article 6 (1) The Regional Government provides services to women and children victims of violence and neglect.
(2) Services as referred to in paragraph (1) are in the form of:
a. complaints; b. health rehabilitation;
c. social rehabilitation;
d. social reintegration; and e. legal assistance and accompaniment.
Article 7 (1) Women and children victims of violence are placed in safe houses or places whose whereabouts are kept confidential and receive basic fulfillment in accordance with their rights.
(2) Child victims of violence who are placed in safe houses are provided with care in accordance with their needs.

CHAPTER II PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 12 (1) Protection of women and children from acts of violence is conducted based on the principles of: a. respect for human rights; b. non-discrimination; and c. protection of victims.
(2) Protection of women and children from acts of violence aims to protect, respect, guarantee the human rights of women and children, and pursue the best interests of women and children.

CHAPTER IX GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 19 (1) The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region.
(2) The community is authorized to actively supervise the implementation of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region.
(3) The authority of the community as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of:
a. providing input; b. submitting questions and obtaining answers from regional government officials who are responsible;
c. requesting realization and concrete activities from those assigned with duties and authority;
d. other matters that are constructive in nature and provide solutions.

CHAPTER XI FUNDING
Article 21
(1) Funding for the Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget.
(2) In addition to funds from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, funding may come from grants or contributions from third parties that are non-binding.

(5) Accountability for the use of funds for the implementation of protection of women and children shall be in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and enforced to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for such women. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, return, and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community.
The protection and empowerment of women and children currently becomes a focus in development. Women and children are usually made into one unit within the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the respective scope of each form of handling, namely women and children do not become a unit. In that context, regionally related to women and children, regional regulations must be present concerning: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. These four regional regulations are a package that must be regulated by the Regional Government in accordance with authority.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL
Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and enforced to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for such women. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, return, and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community.
The protection and empowerment of women and children currently becomes a focus in development. Women and children are usually made into one unit within the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the respective scope of each form of handling, namely women and children do not become a unit. In that context, regionally related to women and children, regional regulations must be present concerning: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. These four regional regulations are a package that must be regulated by the Regional Government in accordance with authority.

CHAPTER II PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 12 (1) Protection of women and children from acts of violence is conducted based on the principles of: a. respect for human rights; b. non-discrimination; and c. protection of victims.
(2) Protection of women and children from acts of violence aims to protect, respect, guarantee the human rights of women and children, and pursue the best interests of women and children.

7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BALANGAN REGENCY NUMBER 3 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and enforced to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for such women. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, return, and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community.
The protection and empowerment of women and children currently becomes a focus in development. Women and children are usually made into one unit within the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the respective scope of each form of handling, namely women and children do not become a unit. In that context, regionally related to women and children, regional regulations must be present concerning: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. These four regional regulations are a package that must be regulated by the Regional Government in accordance with authority.

CHAPTER VII INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS
Article 10
(1) In order to provide services to women and children victims of violence, neglect and human trafficking, the Regional Government establishes an Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A).
(2) The Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) is positioned as an independent institution.
Article 11
(1) The Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) has the authority to administer protection for women and children.
(2) The duty of the Regional Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) is to implement protection for women and children in accordance with the provisions stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
Article 12
The membership of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) consists of elements from related agencies, vertical institutions, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, researchers, academics and religious figures, customary figures, community figures and activists for the protection of women and children in the region.
Article 13
(1) The Regent establishes the Management of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A).
(2) The establishment of the Management as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Regent's Decree including the secretariat structure of the management and provision of supporting facilities for the implementation of activities.
Article 14
(1) The Management of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) consists of leadership elements and members stipulated by Regent's Decree.
(2) Leadership elements comprise:
a. chairperson;
b. secretary; and
c. treasurer.
(3) Membership elements are divided into the form of:
a. service division;
b. information division;
c. assistance division;
d. education and training division.
Article 15
(1) The Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children, in carrying out its functions, builds a working network with:
a. Police;
b. Prosecutor's Office;
c. Court;
d. Witness and Victim Protection Institution;
e. Hospital/Community Health Center;
f. Other institutions that have similar objectives.
(2) In addition to building a working network as referred to in paragraph (1), cooperation may be conducted with:
a. Government;
b. Provincial Government;
c. Other Regency/City Governments; and
d. Non-Governmental Institutions.
e. International institutions whose existence is recognized.
(3) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is set forth in the form of a joint agreement.
Article 16
(1) The Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children establishes partnerships with the business sector for support in administering protection for women and children in the Regional territory.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are in the form of:
a. information and opening of employment opportunities;
b. provision of education and job training;
c. provision of educational assistance for women and children victims of violence; and
d. provision of capital assistance for independent businesses.
Article 17
The Regent as the person responsible for the protection and empowerment of regional women and children has the authority to make changes to the management or dismissal of members if the existing management or members do not carry out their roles and functions.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Balangan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Head hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Balangan Regency.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the regional people's representative institution of Balangan Regency which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Office or Agency is an Office or Agency whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the field of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region.
6. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
8. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
9. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a direct line upward or downward and a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child.
10. Parent is a biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
11. Protection of women and children is an effort to prevent and handle all forms of acts of violence including neglect and trafficking in persons that violate the human rights of women and children, as well as providing basic and specific services for the needs of women and children in the conditions and situations they experience.
12. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
13. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Empowerment of women and children is an effort to strengthen human rights, improve quality of life and increase the participation of women and children in their social interactions.
15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
17. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
18. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
21. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related offices, vertical agencies, and the community, in the context of implementing activities for the prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Balangan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Head hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Balangan Regency.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the regional people's representative institution of Balangan Regency which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Office or Agency is an Office or Agency whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the field of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region.
6. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
8. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
9. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a direct line upward or downward and a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child.
10. Parent is a biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
11. Protection of women and children is an effort to prevent and handle all forms of acts of violence including neglect and trafficking in persons that violate the human rights of women and children, as well as providing basic and specific services for the needs of women and children in the conditions and situations they experience.
12. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
13. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Empowerment of women and children is an effort to strengthen human rights, improve quality of life and increase the participation of women and children in their social interactions.
15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
17. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
18. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
21. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related offices, vertical agencies, and the community, in the context of implementing activities for the prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.

CHAPTER X REGIONAL ACTION PLAN
Article 20 (1) The Regent may establish a regional action plan related to the protection and empowerment of women and children.
(2) The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1) is manifested in the joint commitment of all elements in the region to implement the protection and empowerment of women and children and eliminate all forms of violence, neglect and human trafficking.

CHAPTER IX GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 19 (1) The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region.
(2) The community is authorized to actively supervise the implementation of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region.
(3) The authority of the community as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of:
a. providing input; b. submitting questions and obtaining answers from regional government officials who are responsible;
c. requesting realization and concrete activities from those assigned with duties and authority;
d. other matters that are constructive in nature and provide solutions.

ELUCIDATION

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BALANGAN REGENCY NUMBER 3 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and enforced to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for such women. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, return, and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community.
The protection and empowerment of women and children currently becomes a focus in development. Women and children are usually made into one unit within the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the respective scope of each form of handling, namely women and children do not become a unit. In that context, regionally related to women and children, regional regulations must be present concerning: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. These four regional regulations are a package that must be regulated by the Regional Government in accordance with authority.

CHAPTER VII INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS
Article 10
(1) In order to provide services to women and children victims of violence, neglect and human trafficking, the Regional Government establishes an Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A).
(2) The Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) is positioned as an independent institution.
Article 11
(1) The Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) has the authority to administer protection for women and children.
(2) The duty of the Regional Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) is to implement protection for women and children in accordance with the provisions stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
Article 12
The membership of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) consists of elements from related agencies, vertical institutions, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, researchers, academics and religious figures, customary figures, community figures and activists for the protection of women and children in the region.
Article 13
(1) The Regent establishes the Management of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A).
(2) The establishment of the Management as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Regent's Decree including the secretariat structure of the management and provision of supporting facilities for the implementation of activities.
Article 14
(1) The Management of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) consists of leadership elements and members stipulated by Regent's Decree.
(2) Leadership elements comprise:
a. chairperson;
b. secretary; and
c. treasurer.
(3) Membership elements are divided into the form of:
a. service division;
b. information division;
c. assistance division;
d. education and training division.
Article 15
(1) The Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children, in carrying out its functions, builds a working network with:
a. Police;
b. Prosecutor's Office;
c. Court;
d. Witness and Victim Protection Institution;
e. Hospital/Community Health Center;
f. Other institutions that have similar objectives.
(2) In addition to building a working network as referred to in paragraph (1), cooperation may be conducted with:
a. Government;
b. Provincial Government;
c. Other Regency/City Governments; and
d. Non-Governmental Institutions.
e. International institutions whose existence is recognized.
(3) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is set forth in the form of a joint agreement.
Article 16
(1) The Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children establishes partnerships with the business sector for support in administering protection for women and children in the Regional territory.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are in the form of:
a. information and opening of employment opportunities;
b. provision of education and job training;
c. provision of educational assistance for women and children victims of violence; and
d. provision of capital assistance for independent businesses.
Article 17
The Regent as the person responsible for the protection and empowerment of regional women and children has the authority to make changes to the management or dismissal of members if the existing management or members do not carry out their roles and functions.

CHAPTER XI FUNDING
Article 21
(1) Funding for the Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget.
(2) In addition to funds from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, funding may come from grants or contributions from third parties that are non-binding.
(3) Technically and for the operation of the Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children, it shall be placed in the budget line of the Agency determined by the Regent.
(4) The allocation of funds by the Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children shall be based on the established work program.
(5) Accountability for the use of funds for the implementation of protection of women and children shall be in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.
Promulgated in Paringin on January 20, 2016

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Balangan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Head hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Balangan Regency.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the regional people's representative institution of Balangan Regency which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Office or Agency is an Office or Agency whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the field of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region.
6. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
8. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
9. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a direct line upward or downward and a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child.
10. Parent is a biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
11. Protection of women and children is an effort to prevent and handle all forms of acts of violence including neglect and trafficking in persons that violate the human rights of women and children, as well as providing basic and specific services for the needs of women and children in the conditions and situations they experience.
12. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
13. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Empowerment of women and children is an effort to strengthen human rights, improve quality of life and increase the participation of women and children in their social interactions.
15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
17. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
18. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
21. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related offices, vertical agencies, and the community, in the context of implementing activities for the prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and enforced to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for such women. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, return, and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community.
The protection and empowerment of women and children currently becomes a focus in development. Women and children are usually made into one unit within the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the respective scope of each form of handling, namely women and children do not become a unit. In that context, regionally related to women and children, regional regulations must be present concerning: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. These four regional regulations are a package that must be regulated by the Regional Government in accordance with authority.

CHAPTER XI FUNDING
Article 21
(1) Funding for the Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget.
(2) In addition to funds from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, funding may come from grants or contributions from third parties that are non-binding.
(3) Technically and for the operation of the Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children, it shall be placed in the budget line of the Agency determined by the Regent.
(4) The allocation of funds by the Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children shall be based on the established work program.
(5) Accountability for the use of funds for the implementation of protection of women and children shall be in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

The membership of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) consists of elements from related agencies, vertical institutions, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, researchers, academics and religious figures, customary figures, community figures and activists for the protection of women and children in the region.

(1) The Regent establishes the Management of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A).

Article 14
(1) The Management of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) consists of leadership elements and members stipulated by Regent's Decree.

a. service division;
b. information division;
c. assistance division;
d. education and training division.
Article 15

b. Prosecutor's Office;
c. Court;

e. Hospital/Community Health Center;
f. Other institutions that have similar objectives.

a. Government;
b. Provincial Government;
c. Other Regency/City Governments; and

(3) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is set forth in the form of a joint agreement.
Article 16
(1) The Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children establishes partnerships with the business sector for support in administering protection for women and children in the Regional territory.

The Regent as the person responsible for the protection and empowerment of regional women and children has the authority to make changes to the management or dismissal of members if the existing management or members do not carry out their roles and functions.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Balangan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Head hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Balangan Regency.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the regional people's representative institution of Balangan Regency which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Office or Agency is an Office or Agency whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the field of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region.
6. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
8. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
9. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a direct line upward or downward and a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child.
10. Parent is a biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
11. Protection of women and children is an effort to prevent and handle all forms of acts of violence including neglect and trafficking in persons that violate the human rights of women and children, as well as providing basic and specific services for the needs of women and children in the conditions and situations they experience.
12. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
13. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Empowerment of women and children is an effort to strengthen human rights, improve quality of life and increase the participation of women and children in their social interactions.
15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
17. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
18. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
21. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related offices, vertical agencies, and the community, in the context of implementing activities for the prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and enforced to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for such women. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, return, and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community.
The protection and empowerment of women and children currently becomes a focus in development. Women and children are usually made into one unit within the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the respective scope of each form of handling, namely women and children do not become a unit. In that context, regionally related to women and children, regional regulations must be present concerning: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. These four regional regulations are a package that must be regulated by the Regional Government in accordance with authority.

CHAPTER IX GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 19 (1) The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region.
(2) The community is authorized to actively supervise the implementation of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region.
(3) The authority of the community as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of:
a. providing input; b. submitting questions and obtaining answers from regional government officials who are responsible;
c. requesting realization and concrete activities from those assigned with duties and authority;
d. other matters that are constructive in nature and provide solutions.

CHAPTER X REGIONAL ACTION PLAN
Article 20 (1) The Regent may establish a regional action plan related to the protection and empowerment of women and children.
(2) The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1) is manifested in the joint commitment of all elements in the region to implement the protection and empowerment of women and children and eliminate all forms of violence, neglect and human trafficking.

CHAPTER VII INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS
Article 10
(1) In order to provide services to women and children victims of violence, neglect and human trafficking, the Regional Government establishes an Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A).
(2) The Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) is positioned as an independent institution.
Article 11
(1) The Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) has the authority to administer protection for women and children.
(2) The duty of the Regional Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) is to implement protection for women and children in accordance with the provisions stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
Article 12
The membership of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) consists of elements from related agencies, vertical institutions, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, researchers, academics and religious figures, customary figures, community figures and activists for the protection of women and children in the region.
Article 13
(1) The Regent establishes the Management of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A).
(2) The establishment of the Management as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Regent's Decree including the secretariat structure of the management and provision of supporting facilities for the implementation of activities.
Article 14
(1) The Management of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) consists of leadership elements and members stipulated by Regent's Decree.
(2) Leadership elements comprise:
a. chairperson;
b. secretary; and
c. treasurer.
(3) Membership elements are divided into the form of:
a. service division;
b. information division;
c. assistance division;
d. education and training division.
Article 15
(1) The Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children, in carrying out its functions, builds a working network with:
a. Police;
b. Prosecutor's Office;
c. Court;
d. Witness and Victim Protection Institution;
e. Hospital/Community Health Center;
f. Other institutions that have similar objectives.
(2) In addition to building a working network as referred to in paragraph (1), cooperation may be conducted with:
a. Government;
b. Provincial Government;
c. Other Regency/City Governments; and
d. Non-Governmental Institutions.
e. International institutions whose existence is recognized.
(3) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is set forth in the form of a joint agreement.
Article 16
(1) The Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children establishes partnerships with the business sector for support in administering protection for women and children in the Regional territory.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are in the form of:
a. information and opening of employment opportunities;
b. provision of education and job training;
c. provision of educational assistance for women and children victims of violence; and
d. provision of capital assistance for independent businesses.
Article 17
The Regent as the person responsible for the protection and empowerment of regional women and children has the authority to make changes to the management or dismissal of members if the existing management or members do not carry out their roles and functions.

CHAPTER XI FUNDING
Article 21
(1) Funding for the Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget.
(2) In addition to funds from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, funding may come from grants or contributions from third parties that are non-binding.
(3) Technically and for the operation of the Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children, it shall be placed in the budget line of the Agency determined by the Regent.
(4) The allocation of funds by the Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children shall be based on the established work program.
(5) Accountability for the use of funds for the implementation of protection of women and children shall be in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF BALANGAN REGENCY NUMBER 3 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and enforced to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for such women. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, return, and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community.
The protection and empowerment of women and children currently becomes a focus in development. Women and children are usually made into one unit within the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the respective scope of each form of handling, namely women and children do not become a unit. In that context, regionally related to women and children, regional regulations must be present concerning: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. These four regional regulations are a package that must be regulated by the Regional Government in accordance with authority.

CHAPTER X REGIONAL ACTION PLAN
Article 20 (1) The Regent may establish a regional action plan related to the protection and empowerment of women and children.
(2) The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1) is manifested in the joint commitment of all elements in the region to implement the protection and empowerment of women and children and eliminate all forms of violence, neglect and human trafficking.

CHAPTER V SERVICES
Article 6 (1) The Regional Government provides services to women and children victims of violence and neglect.
(2) Services as referred to in paragraph (1) are in the form of:
a. complaints; b. health rehabilitation;
c. social rehabilitation;
d. social reintegration; and e. legal assistance and accompaniment.
Article 7 (1) Women and children victims of violence are placed in safe houses or places whose whereabouts are kept confidential and receive basic fulfillment in accordance with their rights.
(2) Child victims of violence who are placed in safe houses are provided with care in accordance with their needs.

CHAPTER IX GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 19 (1) The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region.
(2) The community is authorized to actively supervise the implementation of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region.
(3) The authority of the community as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of:
a. providing input; b. submitting questions and obtaining answers from regional government officials who are responsible;
c. requesting realization and concrete activities from those assigned with duties and authority;
d. other matters that are constructive in nature and provide solutions.

CHAPTER VII INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS
Article 10
(1) In order to provide services to women and children victims of violence, neglect and human trafficking, the Regional Government establishes an Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A).
(2) The Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) is positioned as an independent institution.
Article 11
(1) The Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) has the authority to administer protection for women and children.
(2) The duty of the Regional Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) is to implement protection for women and children in accordance with the provisions stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
Article 12
The membership of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) consists of elements from related agencies, vertical institutions, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, researchers, academics and religious figures, customary figures, community figures and activists for the protection of women and children in the region.
Article 13
(1) The Regent establishes the Management of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A).
(2) The establishment of the Management as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Regent's Decree including the secretariat structure of the management and provision of supporting facilities for the implementation of activities.
Article 14
(1) The Management of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) consists of leadership elements and members stipulated by Regent's Decree.
(2) Leadership elements comprise:
a. chairperson;
b. secretary; and
c. treasurer.
(3) Membership elements are divided into the form of:
a. service division;
b. information division;
c. assistance division;
d. education and training division.
Article 15
(1) The Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children, in carrying out its functions, builds a working network with:
a. Police;
b. Prosecutor's Office;
c. Court;
d. Witness and Victim Protection Institution;
e. Hospital/Community Health Center;
f. Other institutions that have similar objectives.
(2) In addition to building a working network as referred to in paragraph (1), cooperation may be conducted with:
a. Government;
b. Provincial Government;
c. Other Regency/City Governments; and
d. Non-Governmental Institutions.
e. International institutions whose existence is recognized.
(3) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is set forth in the form of a joint agreement.
Article 16
(1) The Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children establishes partnerships with the business sector for support in administering protection for women and children in the Regional territory.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are in the form of:
a. information and opening of employment opportunities;
b. provision of education and job training;
c. provision of educational assistance for women and children victims of violence; and
d. provision of capital assistance for independent businesses.
Article 17
The Regent as the person responsible for the protection and empowerment of regional women and children has the authority to make changes to the management or dismissal of members if the existing management or members do not carry out their roles and functions.

CHAPTER XI FUNDING
Article 21
(1) Funding for the Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget.
(2) In addition to funds from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, funding may come from grants or contributions from third parties that are non-binding.
(3) Technically and for the operation of the Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children, it shall be placed in the budget line of the Agency determined by the Regent.
(4) The allocation of funds by the Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children shall be based on the established work program.
(5) Accountability for the use of funds for the implementation of protection of women and children shall be in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.
